assessment.nobel_worthiness: GLP-1 physiology from proglucagon processing and incretin action to peptide therapeutics is a coherent, original line of work that has changed treatment of type 2 diabetes and obesity and opened broad cardiometabolic benefit. Impact is exceptionally large and clearly documented.
assessment.attribution: Holst (physiology and secretion of the active GLP-1 forms), Drucker (biology of GLP-1 and GLP-2 and translation) and Mojsov (identification of the bioactive peptide and its synthesis) form a defensible trio on the science side. Knudsen's drug-design contribution is substantial but is partly industrial and would be the first person left out; credit between basic and drug-development contributions is unresolved.
assessment.maturity: Several clinical outcome trials and widespread real-world use confirm efficacy independently; recognition is timely and arguably overdue given the scale of use.
uncertainties: Whether the committee prefers to honor the drug-development contribution (Knudsen) over one of the physiology contributors.
Priority disputes around the early identification of active GLP-1(7-36) and the role of other groups not credited here.
My knowledge of the attribution history is from memory and not independently verified.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optogenetics gave a general, genetically targeted way to control and probe cell activity with light and transformed causal neuroscience, with spread into cardiac, retinal and other physiology. Originality and breadth of influence are very high.
assessment.attribution: Channelrhodopsin discovery and characterization (Nagel, Hegemann, with Bamberg) and its deployment for controlling neurons (Deisseroth, Boyden) are both decisive, as are Miesenböck's earlier genetically targeted photoactivation concepts. Six credited names cannot fit within three; this is a genuine allocation problem and the trio chosen omits Bamberg, Boyden and Miesenböck.
assessment.maturity: Two decades of independent confirmation and ubiquitous use; first clinical applications (retinal optogenetic vision restoration) are emerging. Timing is mature for the research tool.
uncertainties: Allocation of credit among six names with real priority arguments.
Therapeutic translation is early, so the case rests on a research-tool discovery.
Attribution details recalled from memory, not verified.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Genetically engineered T cells directed at tumor antigens created a new class of living therapy that induces durable remissions in refractory B-cell malignancies. The principle is clear and impactful and extends to other diseases.
assessment.attribution: June (clinical CD19 CAR-T with costimulation, CLL and ALL), Sadelain (costimulatory CAR design and preclinical foundation) and Rosenberg (adoptive cell transfer and early gene-engineered T cells) are a plausible configuration. Eshhar's original chimeric receptor concept is not in the supplied credit list, which weakens the allocation.
assessment.maturity: Multiple approved products and long follow-up from independent centers confirm efficacy; limits in solid tumors and toxicity remain but do not alter the core discovery.
uncertainties: Whether the foundational chimeric-receptor concept is adequately represented by the supplied names.
Durability and safety data are still accruing for long-term cure claims.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Splice-switching antisense oligonucleotides correcting SMN2 exon 7 inclusion led to nusinersen, a transformative treatment for spinal muscular atrophy and a proof of concept for RNA-targeted therapy.
assessment.attribution: Krainer (mechanistic definition of the SMN2 splicing target) and Bennett (antisense chemistry and drug development) form a clean pair; credit seems comparatively clear, though others contributed to SMN gene discovery and to the underlying oligonucleotide chemistry.
assessment.maturity: Approved drug with years of independent clinical follow-up; the mechanistic and clinical story is stable and well confirmed.
uncertainties: Contributions of the SMN gene discovery and antisense chemistry fields could be argued as part of a broader compound discovery.
Part of the credit is industrial/translational.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The unfolded protein response defined a new form of organelle-to-nucleus signaling (IRE1, HAC1/XBP1 splicing) with consequences for secretory physiology, diabetes, neurodegeneration and cancer. A conceptually original and fundamental cell-biological discovery.
assessment.attribution: Walter and Mori are the central, well-recognized pair for identification of the pathway and its mechanism; credit is comparatively clear, with other contributors (such as Ron and colleagues on PERK/ATF6 branches) outside the supplied list.
assessment.maturity: Decades of independent confirmation and extensive follow-up; the core pathway is stable. Disease-therapeutic translation is still developing, so impact is more foundational than clinical.
uncertainties: Whether the committee would find the discovery more conceptual than medically transformative.
Credit for the additional UPR branches is outside the supplied names.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: BCL-2 as the founding member of the apoptosis-regulating family, from translocation-driven lymphoma to the anti-apoptotic function, explained how cell survival is controlled and led to BH3 mimetics such as venetoclax.
assessment.attribution: Cory and Adams drove the cloning and functional characterization; Vaux showed that BCL-2 blocks cell death rather than promoting proliferation, a decisive conceptual step. Strasser is also a major contributor, and the Tsujimoto, Korsmeyer and Horvitz contributions overlap with already recognized apoptosis work, complicating credit.
assessment.maturity: Mature and independently confirmed, with an approved targeted therapy. Recognition would build on the earlier apoptosis prize, which may reduce perceived novelty.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2002 prize on programmed cell death and credit sharing with others not supplied.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Culture of self-organizing organoids from single adult Lgr5-positive stem cells created a widely used platform for studying tissue renewal, disease modeling, host-pathogen interaction and personalized drug testing.
assessment.attribution: Clevers (Lgr5 stem cells and the organoid concept) and Sato (the first intestinal organoid culture) are decisive; the credit is relatively concise. Other organoid lineages, such as pluripotent-derived organoids, are not captured here.
assessment.maturity: Broad independent adoption over about 15 years; clinical translation is still emerging, and impact is currently mainly as a research platform.
uncertainties: Whether recognition should cover pluripotent-stem-cell organoids as well.
Clinical benefit is not yet established.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: BCL11A as a repressor of fetal hemoglobin, derived from human genetics, led to a gene-editing therapy that reactivates fetal hemoglobin in sickle cell disease and beta-thalassemia. It is a clear path from human genetics to mechanism and cure.
assessment.attribution: Orkin and Sankaran led the mechanism and BCL11A work; Thein contributed to the human genetic modifiers of fetal hemoglobin. Bauer's enhancer targeting was key to the therapeutic design, so four names compete for three places.
assessment.maturity: Therapy approved only recently with limited long-term follow-up, so recognition may be somewhat premature although the mechanism is firm.
uncertainties: Short follow-up of the editing therapy.
Four credited names for three spots and possible need to recognize earlier fetal hemoglobin genetics.
